observations.description: Original 3D cartoon animation in the same character style: medieval palace, army, city gate; key prop (bronze dragon jar with frogs) recurs throughout.
Close-up inserts on the key prop (dragon mouth, frog) alternate with wide establishing shots (palace hall, army, city).
Time-of-day lighting tells the story: warm sunset, blue moonlit night, orange dust cloud for the earthquake.

Captions show 1-2 words at a time in sentence case with punctuation kept (e.g. 'Wait,', 'paradise.'); white heavy rounded sans-serif with a thin dark outline and soft shadow, centred just below the middle of the frame. No boxes, no emoji.
Font category: heavy geometric/rounded sans-serif (Poppins/Montserrat-like category). The exact font cannot be identified from the frames.
Historical mystery told as a mini-story; the final sentence is the reveal (the earthquake) and the video ends right after it.
Hook is a single concrete paradox stated immediately: "He put a bronze ball in a dragon's mouth and told the emperor, if this ever falls out, run!"
Ends on a concrete payoff that resolves the hook, no call to action: "All eight meant the biggest earthquake the empire had ever seen was right underneath them."

categorical.hook_style: one-sentence concrete paradox (strange action, absurd consequence, or rule + contradiction), no intro
categorical.ending_style: concrete payoff image that resolves the hook, then the video stops (no CTA, no summary)
